feedback.problem: Determine the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=y\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)$ at the point $(0,-2,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)) \\  & =\frac{2xy}{{x}^{2}+1} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(0,-2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(0,-2) & =\frac{2(0)(-2)}{{0}^{2}+1}=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(0,-2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({0}^{2}+1)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-0 & =(x-0)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(0,-2)+(y-(-2))\frac{∂f}{∂y}(0,-2) \\ z & =0x+0(y+2) \\ z & =0\end{aligned}
$$
